name.en: Fake HMRC tax refund: “claim your rebate now”

how.en: A text or email that looks like it is from HMRC says you are due a tax refund or rebate. It gives a link to “claim” it before a deadline. The link goes to a fake site that asks for your personal and bank or card details. HMRC never tells you about a refund, or asks you to claim one, by text, email or phone.

text.en: A text or email says it is from HMRC and that you are owed a tax refund.
It says you must claim it soon or you will lose it.
It gives a link to a page that looks like GOV.UK.
The page asks for your bank or card details “to pay the refund”.
HMRC: You are eligible for a tax refund of £326.40. Claim before midnight or it will be cancelled: [link]
Dear Customer, after the last annual calculation of your fiscal activity we have determined that you are eligible to receive a tax rebate. Please submit your claim within 48 hours: [link]

en: HMRC writing by text or email to offer a refund or rebate.
A link and a short deadline to claim.
A page asking for card or bank details to “receive” money.
Don’t click the link or reply.
Check what you are owed in your HMRC online account or the official HMRC app.
Forward suspicious texts to 60599 and emails to HMRC’s phishing address.
If you gave bank or card details, call your bank straight away (you can dial 159).
